fields.Front: Who published the first work on packet switching, and when?
fields.Back: Leonard Kleinrock at MIT, 1961 (using queueing theory to show packet switching's effectiveness for bursty traffic). Paul Baran (RAND) and Donald Davies (NPL, UK) developed the idea independently.

fields.Front: What was the ARPAnet, and when and where was its first packet switch installed?
fields.Back: The first packet-switched computer network and direct ancestor of the Internet; the first packet switch was installed at UCLA in 1969 (four nodes by end of 1969).

fields.Text: The first packet switch of the ARPAnet was installed at {{c1::UCLA}} in {{c2::1969}}; the first email program was written by {{c3::Ray Tomlinson}} in 1972.

fields.Front: Who designed the architecture for interconnecting networks ('internetting') that led to TCP/IP?
fields.Back: Vinton Cerf and Robert Kahn (1974); TCP, UDP and IP were conceptually in place by the end of the 1970s.

fields.Front: What was ALOHAnet's contribution, and who built on it to create Ethernet?
fields.Back: ALOHAnet (Hawaii, Abramson) introduced the first multiple-access protocol for a shared radio medium; Metcalfe and Boggs built on it to develop Ethernet (1976).

fields.Text: {{c1::TCP/IP}} was officially deployed on ARPAnet on {{c2::January 1, 1983}}, replacing {{c3::NCP}}.

fields.Front: Who invented the World Wide Web, where, and what were its four key components?
fields.Back: Tim Berners-Lee at CERN, 1989-1991: HTML, HTTP, a Web server, and a browser.

fields.Text: The Web was invented by {{c1::Tim Berners-Lee}} at {{c2::CERN}} (1989-1991).
fields.Extra: Its four components: HTML, HTTP, a web server, a browser.

fields.Front: What were the four 'killer applications' of the Internet by the end of the 1990s?
fields.Back: Email, the Web, instant messaging, and peer-to-peer file sharing (Napster).
